question: What flow in the space of Riemannian metrics is induced when a neural network representing the metric is trained by gradient descent, when can that flow reproduce Ricci flow, and why do finite neural Calabi-Yau metric models outperform fixed kernels?

key_findings.claim: The metric-NTK equation is a useful function-space organization of neural metric training, but its most general form follows directly from the chain rule.
key_findings.evidence: Differentiating g_theta with respect to training time and substituting parameter gradient flow gives a bi-local kernel formed by parameter Jacobian products. This metric-NTK couples the update at x to loss variation at x-prime, generally evolves with parameters, mixes metric components, and is not an ordinary rank-four tensor because its index pairs live at different points.

key_findings.claim: Perelman Ricci flow is realized only as a formal continuum, infinite-width, zero-bandwidth special case, not as the finite neural method evaluated in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: The construction first takes network width to infinity so the NTK freezes, assigns independent networks to metric components, engineers a Gaussian kernel using frozen random cosine features, then sends its coordinate-frequency scale to infinity so the bandwidth tends to zero. Locality is meaningful only with an integral over the whole manifold; for discrete training points a delta kernel cannot update unseen points. Choosing a Perelman-functional loss then produces the local gradient-flow expression.

anchors.section: 2.4 Ricci Flow and More General Flows

key_findings.claim: The local architecture is not shown to define a coordinate-invariant, globally positive-definite Riemannian metric flow.
key_findings.evidence: Its locality kernel uses Euclidean coordinate differences inside one R-d chart and a fixed reference determinant; the paper notes that the component Kronecker deltas amount to a gauge choice not preserved by diffeomorphisms. Independent component networks do not by themselves enforce positive definiteness. In the numerical implementation, metrics from 20 possible coordinate choices cannot be mixed, so the authors oversample roughly twenty-fold and reject points until all retained metrics share one coordinate system.

anchors.section: 2.3.1 Architecture Design for Local Metric Flow

key_findings.claim: The fixed kernels interpolate the training set spectacularly but fail to learn an efficient off-sample Calabi-Yau metric.
key_findings.evidence: Gaussian and nearest-neighbor Delta kernels improve sigma loss by about one million-fold when test points coincide with training points, yet actual held-out experiments at roughly one thousand and one hundred thousand training points improve test loss by only about five-fold. Prior finite three-layer neural models on 100k points report ten-to-one-hundred-fold validation improvement, consistent with a real fixed-kernel generalization gap.

key_findings.claim: The astronomical sample-complexity estimates are extrapolations from proxy points, not measured requirements.
key_findings.evidence: To vary distance, Gaussian noise is added to training points, explicitly moving test points only approximately onto the Calabi-Yau. A power law for mean nearest distance is then fit over a few point counts and combined with the proxy loss-distance curve to project 100-fold gains at 10^8 Delta or 10^12 Gaussian points and million-fold gains at 10^35 points. These ranges are many orders beyond the direct 10^3 and 10^5 tests.

key_findings.claim: The metric-NTK evolution plot shows departure from the lazy regime but does not establish that feature learning caused the finite network's accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: The diagnostic uses only ten fixed train and ten fixed test points. It computes eigenvalues separately for each of 81 component blocks and pools them, rather than diagonalizing the full positive-semidefinite kernel over joint component-point indices; off-diagonal blocks need not have meaningful real spectra. No width sweep, frozen-feature finite network, kernel-learning ablation, or correlation between NTK movement and held-out sigma loss is reported.

anchors.section: 3.3 Calabi-Yau Metric Learning and NTK Evolution

key_findings.claim: The scalability workaround introduces an uncontrolled block-diagonal approximation.
key_findings.evidence: The full metric-NTK at 100k points would have nearly a trillion entries. The proposed batched agglomerative clustering forms approximately 5k-point clusters and neglects all cross-cluster kernel contributions. Its reported silhouette scores are 0.016 for batched and -0.011 for full clustering, both essentially zero, and performance sensitivity to this omission is not ablated.

method.core_idea: Push neural-network parameter gradient flow through the metric output map to obtain a kernel gradient flow on metric functions, then study infinite-width and locality limits and compare their fixed kernels with finite neural Calabi-Yau metric learning.
method.mechanism: The metric-NTK is the inner product of parameter Jacobians of metric components at two manifold points. Infinite-width linearization freezes this kernel. Independent component networks eliminate component mixing; a random-cosine last-layer kernel approaches a coordinate delta function as its frequency variance grows, and a tailored loss formally recovers Perelman flow. Numerically, clustered ReLU-NTK, Gaussian, and nearest-neighbor kernels iteratively update Hermitian metrics under sigma loss.
assumptions: The network output remains a valid symmetric or Hermitian positive-definite metric during its flow.
A chosen coordinate gauge and fixed reference volume form suffice for the desired global geometric interpretation.
Infinite-width lazy dynamics accurately represent the proposed fixed-kernel baselines.
Cross-cluster kernel interactions can be neglected after Fubini-Study-distance clustering.
Ambient Fubini-Study distance is a useful proxy for unknown Calabi-Yau geodesic distance.
Movement of an empirical NTK diagnostic is evidence of task-relevant feature learning.

techniques.role: Expresses metric-component updates as a bi-local kernel gradient flow.
Freezes the metric kernel in an infinite-width linearized regime.
Uses independent component networks and random cosine features to engineer a local Gaussian-to-delta kernel.
Selects an energy functional so the local kernel flow matches a desired geometric gradient flow.
Approximates the infeasible full kernel with Fubini-Study-distance blocks.
Tracks pooled component-block eigenvalues during finite-network training as a feature-learning diagnostic.

evaluations.setting: Fermat quintic metric learning for frozen ReLU-NTK, Gaussian, and nearest-neighbor Delta kernels.
evaluations.metric: Multiplicative improvement in sigma loss on training-like and held-out points after 50 updates.
evaluations.result: Gaussian and Delta kernels nearly solve training points but all tested fixed kernels improve true test loss by at most about five-fold.
evaluations.baseline: Prior finite ReLU networks reported as improving validation loss by roughly ten-to-one-hundred-fold.

evaluations.setting: Noise-perturbed points at varying ambient Fubini-Study distance from sampled training points.
evaluations.metric: Sigma-loss gain versus nearest distance and nearest-distance scaling with point count.
evaluations.result: Kernel gains decay rapidly with distance; a fitted N^-0.184 distance law is used for far-out sample-count projections.

evaluations.setting: Batched clustering on 1,000 illustrative points and ten clusters.
evaluations.result: Batched clustering produces visible ordering but a near-zero silhouette of 0.016; full clustering is -0.011 and Birch -0.032.
evaluations.baseline: No clustering, full agglomerative clustering, and Euclidean Birch clustering.

evaluations.setting: Three-layer 128-unit GELU multiplicative cymetric network for 50 epochs.
evaluations.metric: Pooled component-block eigenvalue histograms and Wasserstein distance from initialization on ten train and ten test points.
evaluations.result: The chosen NTK summary changes markedly late in training.
evaluations.baseline: The same network's initialization; no matched frozen-feature causal control.

limitations: The Ricci-flow realization is a formal continuum special case and is not executed or benchmarked as the proposed neural architecture.
Coordinate delta kernels and independent component networks are not shown to patch into a globally diffeomorphism-covariant construction.
Positive definiteness is not architectural; Gaussian updates can produce indefinite matrices and clipping degrades performance.
The full kernel is replaced by independent clusters despite near-zero silhouette scores and no approximation-error bound.
All numerical results use one Fermat-quintic benchmark and a sigma-loss target.
No repeated runs, error bars, compute matching, or controlled finite-versus-frozen architecture comparison is reported.
Distance-controlled pseudo-test points leave the manifold, and giant sample-complexity estimates extrapolate far beyond observations.
The empirical NTK spectrum is built from separate component blocks rather than the full joint kernel and is not tied causally to accuracy.
failure_modes: A local coordinate update fails to transform consistently across chart overlaps.
Independent metric-component predictions yield an indefinite matrix and cease to define a Riemannian metric.
A narrow Gaussian kernel memorizes samples while producing negligible updates at typical held-out distances.
Discarded cross-cluster interactions remove the only paths by which a nonlocal kernel could generalize.
Bayesian optimization overfits kernel hyperparameters to a sampled point cloud despite regenerating clouds between runs.
An evolving NTK reflects scale drift or component coupling rather than useful representation learning.
Ambient distance groups geometrically dissimilar points or separates intrinsically nearby ones.
reusable_insights: For models that output geometric tensors, analyze the Jacobian kernel as a bi-tensor and test coordinate transformations explicitly.
Local delta kernels cannot generalize from discrete samples; locality is compatible with learning only when the loss covers the continuum or a separate interpolation mechanism exists.
Enforce symmetry and positive definiteness by parameterization before interpreting an output as a metric.
Compare the full joint NTK spectrum or invariant kernel statistics, not pooled spectra of nonsymmetric component blocks.
A feature-learning claim needs matched frozen-feature controls and a link between representation movement and held-out error.
Do not turn a short-range nearest-neighbor curve into astronomical sample-complexity claims without on-manifold tests and uncertainty bounds.
open_questions: Can a globally chart-consistent, positive-definite neural metric parameterization admit a tractable metric-NTK flow?
Can learned low-rank or inducing-point kernels retain nonlocal generalization without trillion-entry tensors?
What full-kernel invariant best measures task-relevant feature learning for Hermitian metric outputs?
Does an architecture-matched finite-versus-lazy width sweep reproduce the reported fixed-kernel gap at equal compute?
Can intrinsic distances be jointly learned with the Calabi-Yau metric without circular instability?
How do symmetry-aware, Grassmannian, and analytic-distillation methods compare on identical manifolds, samples, and Ricci-flatness metrics?
Is there a finite-bandwidth geometric flow with provable generalization and chart covariance that outperforms both Ricci flow and generic MLPs?

competitive_landscape.title: Calabi-Yau Metrics through Grassmannian Learning and Donaldson's Algorithm
competitive_landscape.difference: Ek, Kim, and Mishra optimize a subspace of algebraic sections directly on a Grassmannian and combine it with Donaldson's algorithm or Hermitian h-matrix learning, preserving more global geometric structure than coordinate-local fixed kernels.

competitive_landscape.title: Symbolic Approximations to Ricci-flat Metrics Via Extrinsic Symmetries of Calabi-Yau Hypersurfaces
competitive_landscape.difference: Mirjanic and Mishra exploit extrinsic symmetries to constrain neural metrics, report state-of-the-art Ricci-curvature reductions, and distill closed-form near-flat metrics, targeting global priors and interpretability absent from metric-NTK kernels.

competitive_landscape.title: Approximate Ricci-flat Metrics for Calabi-Yau Manifolds
competitive_landscape.difference: Lee and Lukas fit ML-computed Kähler potentials into Donaldson's ansatz to obtain relatively simple analytic expressions across Dwork and bicubic families, whereas Metric Flows remains a kernel-dynamics explanation on one quintic.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Group Invariant Calabi-Yau Metrics by Fundamental Domain Projections
competitive_landscape.difference: Hendi, Larfors, and Walden add nontrainable canonicalization layers that guarantee discrete group invariance and improve phi-model accuracy, offering an explicit geometric inductive bias rather than inferring useful structure from NTK evolution.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Network Approximations for Calabi-Yau Metrics
competitive_landscape.difference: Jejjala, Mayorga Pena, and Mishra directly learn Ricci-flat metrics on several two- and three-dimensional Calabi-Yau manifolds and evaluate curvature reductions; Metric Flows chiefly explains why such finite models may beat lazy kernels.

competitive_landscape.title: CYJAX: A Package for Calabi-Yau Metrics with JAX
competitive_landscape.difference: CYJAX provides practical differentiable tooling for learning Calabi-Yau metrics; it is a more deployment-oriented baseline for scalability and metric-validity checks than the paper's bespoke clustered fixed-kernel updates.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Neural gradient descent induces a general metric-NTK flow; Perelman Ricci flow is a highly constrained local infinite-width member, while successful finite Calabi-Yau models rely on evolving-kernel feature learning unavailable to fixed kernels.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper derives the bi-local update, constructs a random-feature Gaussian-to-delta architecture, shows fixed kernels memorize but generalize poorly on the Fermat quintic, and observes an empirical kernel summary change during finite training.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The metric-NTK framing and explicit location of Ricci flow inside a wider family are conceptually original. The empirical explanation is suggestive rather than causal, and the geometric realization is much narrower than the rhetoric: it lacks global chart covariance and positivity guarantees, the scalable kernel approximation is uncontrolled, and the NTK diagnostic is not the spectrum of the full joint kernel.

reviewer_notes: Read all 36 pages, including the neural-network primer, Kähler-flow appendix, and every reference. Visually inspected Figures 1-4 and Table 1; Figure 2 confirms near-zero clustering quality despite visual ordering, Figure 3 confirms the proxy-distance extrapolation, and Figure 4 confirms pooled blockwise rather than full-kernel spectra. Primary arXiv competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
